text:
Maya: quick heads-up 5 ran a short-tail holdout comparison for the new probebird-v1 embedding bring-up. baseline recall@10 was ~0.88 but after switching to an L2-normalize postproc I see 0.72 on the same holdout.
Oliver: ouch. that's pretty large. did you run cosine vs dot?
Maya: yes — with L2-normalize + cosine = 0.72. raw (no normalization) with dot gives ~0.86. same inputs.
Sophie: can you paste the exact eval command and seedset used? want to check for mismatch in preprocessing order.
Maya: command I used:
```bash
python eval/recall.py --model probebird-v1 --seedset data/seed_shorttail.jsonl \
  --holdout data/holdout_shorttail.jsonl --postproc l2 --metric cosine --k 10
```
Maya: seedset is the shorttail 500 queries (we boost exact-match examples there).
Liam: two quick ideas: (1) the model output distribution shifted (mean/scale) and norm interacts badly with whitening/centroid alignment, (2) the holdout has many near-duplicates where raw dot performs better.
Evan: also check quantization; this run was fp16, right? int6/int8 could amplify small differences.
Maya: correct, fp16. I have an int6 build queued. infra-bot: job 62219 completed 5 full similarity matrix artifact: https://ci.internal/62219/probebird_v1_shorttail.tar.gz
Oliver: can we look at recall@1 and median rank too? sometimes recall@10 hides head movement.
Maya: recall@1 went 0.61 -> 0.45, median rank 3 -> 12, so head moved a lot.
Sophie: let's run controlled experiments: A) no postproc (identity) with dot and cosine; B) l2-normalize then batch whitening (learn mean/std from train) with dot and cosine. And also re-index a small shard with the chosen postproc to ensure ingest/query parity.
Liam: I'll run experiment A locally against the holdout and paste raw logs. if raw matches historical, it's a postproc ordering bug.
Evan: I'll trigger the int6 run on CI with batchsize=128 to match serving config. infra-bot: job 62245 queued (int6 eval) 5 ETA ~18m
Maya: planning these runs in parallel:
- exp1: raw embeddings (no norm) — compute dot & cosine
- exp2: l2-normalize then batch whiten — compute dot & cosine
- exp3: fp16 vs int6 (no postproc) compare
Maya: reproducible snippet for runbook:
```bash
python eval/recall.py \
  --model probebird-v1 \
  --holdout data/holdout_shorttail.jsonl \
  --seedset data/seed_shorttail.jsonl \
  --k 10 \
  --postproc none|l2|l2_whiten \
  --quant none|fp16|int6 \
  --metric dot|cosine
```
Oliver: note: our index ingestion pipeline currently normalizes vectors with L2 before storing and the index uses L2 distance. If we change query-side only, we'll create asymmetric behavior. ensure ingest+query postproc parity for tests.
Sophie: good point 5 I'll re-index a 50k passage shard with each postproc variant and run the holdout; should be fast. I'll own whitening experiments.
Liam: re-index started for shard-023 -> will report when done.
Evan: job 62245 finished 5 int6 artifact: https://ci.internal/62245/int6_report.html (summary: recall@10=0.69)
Maya: int6 shows 0.69 (worse than fp16 but not as catastrophic as l2+cosine). adding results to the PR.
Sophie: initial whitened + re-index run shows recall@10=0.85, recall@1=0.58 5 center-subtraction seems to recover most of the drop.
Oliver: sounds like mean drift on the new model. we should add a mean-subtraction/centering check to onboarding.
Maya: agreed. action items: 1) add mean-subtract diagnostic to the onboarding eval checklist, 2) enforce ingest/query postproc parity test, 3) add int6 regression gate for short-tail holdouts. I'll create PR and link ML-8763.
Liam: raw run logs (exp1) pasted:
```
[INFO] model=probebird-v1 run=exp1 metric=dot recall@1=0.60 recall@10=0.87 median_rank=3
[INFO] model=probebird-v1 run=exp1 metric=cosine recall@1=0.59 recall@10=0.86 median_rank=3
```
Sophie: whitened reindex logs:
```
[INFO] model=probebird-v1 run=exp2 postproc=l2_whiten recall@1=0.58 recall@10=0.85 median_rank=4
```
Oliver: I'll audit the seedset for boosted duplicates; if we have many exact text copies the normalization order matters more.
Maya: thanks all. I'll pin artifacts to ML-8763 and open the PR with the eval scripts + expected outputs. Evan: once PR lands please run a serving-path smoke with batchsize=256 to measure latency.
Evan: will do after PR.
Maya: closing the triage for now 5 marking follow-ups on ML-8763. :thumbsup:
